title: Hydrolox component audit for OTA-TEC-0085 RL-25 class
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0085 component draft. Using primary manufacturer, NASA/ESA/JAXA and peer-reviewed propulsion sources, assess: (1) real vacuum specific impulse ranges for RL10-family and other high-performance LH2/LOX engines; (2) real thrust ranges and whether any demonstrated or well-supported hydrolox vacuum engine combines approximately 450 kN thrust with approximately 465 s vacuum Isp; (3) whether such a combination is physically plausible as a 2040s fictional advanced chemical engine and what cycle, nozzle expansion, chamber-pressure, mass, cooling, materials and lifetime constraints would dominate; (4) restartability and lifetime considerations for a reusable cislunar upper-stage engine; (5) whether a four-engine cluster creates meaningful engine-out capability across TLI/LOI/correction burns or only in selected mission phases; and (6) wording that should be narrowed or reclassified in the source dossier. Do not classify the combination as [F] merely because no current serial engine matches it. Distinguish explicitly between [R] = demonstrated/directly supported, [H] = not demonstrated as this exact engine but physically and technically supportable by a stated extrapolation path, [F] = work-set fiction not defensible as a grounded technical extrapolation, and [OFFEN] = evidence insufficient. Any [H] conclusion must name the enabling technical path and limiting constraints rather than relying on generic future-technology language. Keep the fictional name RL-25, the 450 kN value, the four-engine CYGNUS configuration and all NOXIA gameplay/balancing values out of automatic correction. Do not treat similarity of names to RL10 or any real engine as identity.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0085 is the first proposed OTA component dossier and its central purpose is to test combined-parameter plausibility before the component schema is frozen or CYGNUS engine data are deduplicated.
real_world_anchor: High-performance LH2/LOX vacuum rocket engines, RL10-family reference data, staged-combustion/expander cycles, nozzle expansion, restartability and engine-out behavior.
novelty_reason: First source-pinned evidence audit of a proposed OTA-TEC component dossier and its combined engine parameters.
